item.title: First Post: My Journey to Launch Shakastats
item.description:
Aloha! Welcome to shakastats my personal blog website to post nerdy statistical projects and posts. Getting this website up and running was a bit of a challenge and looking back took a lot longer than needed. I wanted to document my overall journey through developing this website and mistakes that I made so you don’t have to.

Learning how to effectively write Quarto documents

This is the number one tip I can give anyone who is used to creating Rmarkdown documents but not quarto documents:

SWITCH YOUR RSTUDIO EDITOR TO “SOURCE” NOT “VISUAL”.

In my job, we often had to write Rmarkdown documents for ad-hoc reports and analyses. I even used Rmarkdown to submit my statistical theory assignments in graduate school. Needless to say, I was extremely comfortable with writing Rmarkdown documents and learned that Quarto is the new and improved version of Rmarkdown.

But it felt extremely clunky… and that was due to visual mode.

In visual mode, a lot of the source code gets “rendered” immediately and I often found myself fighting the visual rendering to produce what I wanted. At least once a day, I wished that I could just write all the source code and click a render button once I was done writing all the source code. By complete accident, I clicked on the source button at the top left of my Rstudio IDE and realized that this was exactly what I needed all along! Now I can zip through writing a file and double check the formatting/rendering once I have most of the code together. This was an embarrassingly obvious feature that cost me an embarrassing amount of development time… but I am very happy that I know this now!

Integrating Quarto documents into a Hugo website… don’t bother with it

My first iteration of this website actually used Hugo instead of Quarto. Although I was comfortable with some basic Quarto and knew about it’s capability in creating websites, I wanted to use Hugo as it seems more prevalent outside of analysis circles. I gone through a few Hugo themes until I found one that I liked from the theme page… and it turns out the website format was pay walled.

Instead of going through the pay wall with money, I tried to instead start with a basic, minimal hugo theme Gokarna. It was nice, but a little too basic and lacked some features I wanted for the website. Additionally, integrating Quarto documents into a Hugo website is admittedly just a few extra steps of rendering files to markdown, but it did feel like a wasted step every time I iterated a new version of the website.

Then I finally pulled the trigger and dove deep into the Quarto documentation for creating a website. A lot of the features out of the box were really useful. In fact, this entire website (in its current iteration) uses a lot of the built in yaml features in Quarto. I haven’t needed to write any custom javascript/html/css yet, but it’s nice that I have this great base that I can iterate on instead of reinventing the wheel.

Some features I particularly like about a Quarto website:

  • Giscus Comments. No need to make a database, just use Github discussions.

  • Adding a citation for reference at the bottom of an article.

  • The categories filtering for articles

New features that I hope to add to the website

One feature I hope to add is a “Preview of upcoming blog posts/articles” that I’m currently working on. I’m not sure how it would work out exactly, but I imagine some sort of schedule with expected posts dates could be useful. I would also hope that there could be a “suggestions” section where people could contribute future topics for projects/blog posts.

Another feature is to get some sort of analytics service for my website so get a general idea if people are reading my content. I know Google Analytics exists, but my cursory reasearch online show open source analytics platforms Umami and Fathom Analytics exist.

That’s all I currently have planned. Overall, moving everything into the Quarto ecosystem as well as making sure I develop in “Source” mode made writing the project so much smoother. Now my focus is mostly on content and not battling the website aspects, and I couldn’t be happier.

Mahalo for reading 🤙🏾!
